desc: Ideation: select the Prim-like min-heap frontier greedy and identify pitfalls: strict inequality, large integer arithmetic, duplicate heap entries, and safety of stopping when the minimum boundary slime is not absorbable.

Implement the complete Python solution using a flattened grid, bytearray visited array, min-heap of (strength, index), strict condition X * s < total, neighbor expansion, stale-entry skipping, and final total output.
Verify the implementation on the three provided samples and edge cases such as 1x1 grid, X=1, all equal strengths, and large X; sample tests passed and edge cases are handled by the same logic.
Confirm correctness proof: any reachable fixed point contains all reachable cells, so absorbing legal boundary cells in min-strength order until the minimum boundary fails is optimal.
